title: Diagnose API CPU saturation without blind restart
trigger: Customer requests become materially slower while responses, readiness, and core dependencies may still remain healthy.
preconditions: capture the affected route, customer scope, release version, HTTP status, request timing, and X-Request-ID
confirm whether the symptom is degradation or hard failure
record the current container/image identity, main process PID, and resource budget before mitigation
check readiness and core dependency health
preserve process and cgroup evidence before restarting or replacing the runtime
diagnostic_steps: measure repeated customer-path requests and compare p50/p95 or equivalent latency with a known healthy baseline
verify release, image, container, and main API process identity have not changed
inspect running processes for unexpected CPU consumers
capture cgroup cpu.stat and compare nr_throttled plus throttled_usec across the degraded window
confirm the configured CPU budget has not changed during the incident
check PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, proxy, readiness, and container health
correlate a degraded-window X-Request-ID through Nginx/API logs, Loki, and Tempo
distinguish resource contention from dependency latency, code regression, malformed configuration, and proxy failure
mitigation_steps: do not restart or redeploy the API when the main runtime is healthy and the offending process can be isolated safely
do not raise timeouts or modify healthy dependencies to hide resource contention
terminate or suspend only the confirmed runaway workload when that action is within L2 authority
preserve the existing application release, image, container, main process, and resource budget when possible
capture the exact process identity and before/after resource evidence for escalation
validation_steps: confirm the offending process is no longer running
repeat the same latency sample and prove material recovery
confirm release, image, container, main API PID, and CPU budget remain unchanged
confirm readiness and core dependency health remain healthy
escalate for preventive resource telemetry, limits, or application safeguards
escalation_boundary: Escalate to application/platform ownership when CPU consumption is caused by runaway application work, process leaks, unsafe background tasks, or missing resource telemetry. Escalate to infrastructure/platform when the configured resource budget itself is insufficient or unexpectedly constrained. Escalate to incident command when saturation affects multiple services or customer paths, no safe targeted mitigation exists, or broader capacity action is required.
